For each patient, I computed baseline tumor SubCellType proportions from Treatment I / Tumor cells and correlated each subtype proportion with tumor regression ratio across 22 patients using Spearman correlation.

Overall, 48 of 91 subtype correlations were positive and 43 were negative. Positive correlation means patients with a higher baseline proportion of that subtype tended to have greater tumor regression; negative correlation means patients with a higher baseline proportion tended to have less regression.

The strongest positive nominal correlations were c82_SMC_MYH11 (rho=0.536, p=0.010), c23_CD8_Tex_LAYN (rho=0.506, p=0.016), c68_Endo_FABP5 (rho=0.502, p=0.017), c10_CD4_Temra_GZMB (rho=0.483, p=0.023), and c13_CD4_Treg_TNFRSF9 (rho=0.470, p=0.027). The most interpretable immune signal is c23_CD8_Tex_LAYN: a higher baseline fraction of exhausted/antigen-experienced CD8 T cells was associated with greater tumor regression, consistent with a pre-existing anti-tumor immune state that may be reinvigorated by PD-1 blockade.

The strongest negative nominal correlation was c87_Goblet_MUC2 (rho=-0.464, p=0.030), followed by c45_PlasmaB_TXNDC5 (rho=-0.353, p=0.107) and c84_Coloncyte_CA2 (rho=-0.351, p=0.110). This suggests that higher baseline goblet/differentiated epithelial-like proportions tended to associate with weaker tumor regression.

None of the 91 subtype correlations survived BH-FDR correction (minimum q=0.452), so these directions should be interpreted as exploratory trends rather than confirmed predictive biomarkers.

criterion_5.reason: Systematically correlated all 91 subtypes with TRR, reporting both rho/p for Spearman and r/p for Pearson, and assembled sorted results.

criterion_6.reason: Identified some expected top subtypes (c23, c13, c68, c87) but missed key negative candidates like c79_Fibro_FAP and c65_Mph_APOE.
